title: NTKMTL: Mitigating Task Imbalance in Multi-Task Learning from Neural Tangent Kernel Perspective
problem_statement: Task imbalance in multi-task learning causes certain tasks to dominate shared parameter updates while other tasks suffer from insufficient optimization due to differing convergence speeds and loss dynamics.
domain: Multi-task learning across multi-task computer vision dense prediction, molecular property regression, facial attribute classification, and multi-task reinforcement learning.
theoretical_framework: Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) theory and spectral analysis of gradient flow ordinary differential equations, which model convergence speeds of individual tasks through the eigenvalues of an extended multi-task NTK matrix.
methodology: NTKMTL constructs an extended Neural Tangent Kernel matrix across tasks and normalizes task loss weights inversely proportional to the square root of the maximum eigenvalue of each task-specific NTK matrix scaled by the average maximum eigenvalue; NTKMTL-SR accelerates computation by calculating the NTK matrix over shared representations rather than full network parameters.

metrics: Average per-task performance drop relative to single-task learning baseline (Δm%)
Semantic segmentation mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) and pixel accuracy
Depth estimation absolute error and relative error
Surface normal mean error, median error, and percentage within angular thresholds (11.25°, 22.5°, 30°)
Mean Absolute Error (MAE) across 11 quantum chemical regression properties
Multi-attribute classification accuracy across 40 facial attributes
Success rate across 10 robotic manipulation tasks

key_findings: The convergence speed of each task in multi-task learning is governed by the eigenvalues of its task-specific Neural Tangent Kernel matrix, leading to spectral bias where tasks with larger eigenvalues dominate training.
Weighting tasks inversely proportional to the square root of their maximum NTK eigenvalue balances convergence speeds across tasks and mitigates task imbalance.

NTKMTL achieves state-of-the-art performance on the NYUv2 dense prediction benchmark with a mean rank of 4.33 and a relative performance drop of -6.99%, outperforming single-task learning across all three tasks.
On the CelebA 40-task benchmark, NTKMTL achieves an overall improvement over single-task learning (Δm% of -0.77%), outperforming all previous multi-task baselines.

NTKMTL-SR uses shared representations to achieve training speeds comparable to loss-oriented linear scalarization while attaining state-of-the-art results on the QM9 11-task regression benchmark (mean rank 4.00, Δm% 30.7%).
NTKMTL generalizes effectively to multi-task reinforcement learning on the Meta-World MT10 benchmark, achieving a 0.96 success rate.
scope_and_delimitations: Evaluated on supervised multi-task learning (2 to 40 tasks) and multi-task reinforcement learning (10 tasks).
Focuses optimization weight derivations primarily on the diagonal task-specific blocks of the extended NTK matrix.
NTKMTL uses mini-batch size n=1 for shared parameter calculations, while NTKMTL-SR uses mini-batch size n=4 on shared representations.

limitations.verbatim_excerpt: In this work, we proposed the extended NTK Ke for MTL as a tool for more comprehensive analysis of training dynamics across tasks. The weight design of our current method mainly focuses on the analysis of the task-specific NTK matrices Kii. The full structure of the extended NTK matrix Ke offers further analytical opportunities. For example, analyzing the off-diagonal Kij blocks could reveal novel insights into task interactions or guide the development of task grouping strategies. These potential avenues are left for future investigation.
limitations.summary: The method relies solely on the diagonal task-specific blocks of the extended NTK matrix rather than modeling inter-task interactions present in the off-diagonal blocks, and NTKMTL-SR is difficult to apply in reinforcement learning settings where networks lack explicit separation between shared and task-specific heads.

generalizability_gap: The method has not been evaluated on large-scale language models, multi-modal foundation models, or non-stationary online learning environments.
methodological_gap: The weight calculation considers only the maximum eigenvalue of the task-specific NTK block rather than the complete eigenvalue spectrum or the off-diagonal task-interaction blocks of the extended NTK matrix.
future_work: Analyzing the off-diagonal blocks Kij of the extended NTK matrix to model inter-task interactions.
Developing task grouping and task clustering strategies based on the full structure of the extended NTK matrix.
Extending shared representation approximations to policy architectures in multi-task reinforcement learning.
